name: 37779-imageprefill-glm4v9b-1gpu
model: zai-org/GLM-4.1V-9B-Thinking -- 20.6 GB of bf16 safetensors, the member of its checkpoint family that fits on one card.
hardware: 1x H100 80GB HBM3 (one GPU of an a3 node, --gres=gpu:1), SM90, driver 570.195.03.
parallelism: TP=1, PP=1, DP=1, one in-process engine (guidellm `vllm_python`), one node, no router and no external cache tier.
architecture: Glm4vForConditionalGeneration: a 40-layer text decoder (32 query / 2 KV heads, hidden 4096, head_dim 128, bf16 -- 40 KiB of KV per token) behind a 24-layer vision tower, patch_size 14, spatial_merge_size 2.
load_profile: concurrent (closed loop), streams=4, warmup the first 25% by completion, bounded at 240 requests with a 1800 s safety cap.
workload: guidellm `synthetic_text` + `synthetic_image`, single turn, one image per request. Image 896x896, jpeg quality 85, `gradient` content, seed 42; text exactly 32 prompt and exactly 32 output tokens (min=max, greedy, ignore_eos). 896 is an exact multiple of the processor's 28-pixel grid (patch_size * spatial_merge_size), so nothing is resized and the patch grid is exactly 64x64 = 4096 vision positions, which the 2x2 merge hands to the decoder as 1024 of the ~1060 prompt tokens. Every request carries a different image: the synthetic image RNG stream advances per row.
purpose: A visual question-answering assistant reading one high-resolution image per short prompt, four concurrent users, single GPU.
launch:
# ENGINE: commit 5dac719b2b5f72d9fbd417c839cb0154607950c0 (v0.18.1rc0-12-g5dac719b2b5f).
# The interpreter and the hardware are in configs/env.yaml; the load is in scenario.json.

model: zai-org/GLM-4.1V-9B-Thinking
tensor-parallel-size: 1
dtype: bfloat16
max-model-len: 4096
max-num-seqs: 8

# Must match scenario.json's `images_per_request: 1` -- it is both the admission limit and what
# the engine's startup profiling pass is sized against. Change one and you must change both.
limit-mm-per-prompt: {"image": 1}

gpu-memory-utilization: 0.90

# Both caches off: every request carries a byte-different image, so neither can hit on the part
# of the prompt that costs anything, and off, every request does the same work.
enable-prefix-caching: false
mm-processor-cache-gb: 0
